Surah Al-Mujaadila ('The Pleading Woman') is a Medinan surah of 22 verses. It was revealed in response to the plea of Khawlah bint Tha'labah concerning the pre-Islamic practice of zihar - a husband declaring his wife as unlawful to him as his mother's back - thereby abolishing the practice. The surah emphasizes Allah's infinite knowledge and power, condemns secret counsels and intrigues, and affirms that those who ally with Allah will prevail.

intro_en: Surah Al-Hashr ('The Gathering') is a Medinan surah of 24 verses. Its name comes from verse 2's reference to the exile of the Jewish tribe of Banu An-Nadîr from Medina after they conspired with the Meccan pagans against the Muslims. The surah condemns the hypocrites for their secret alliance with them and gives instructions on the distribution of the spoils of war.

intro_en: Surah As-Saff ('The Rank') is a Medinan surah of 14 verses. It takes its name from the command to strive in Allah's cause in solid battle formations in verse 4. The surah urges striving in Allah's cause and supporting His messengers, criticizing those who say what they do not do, and citing the disciples of Jesus as an example.

intro_en: Surah Al-Jumu'a ('Friday') is a Medinan surah of 11 verses. It is named for the Friday congregational prayer addressed in verse 9, which the believers are urged to hasten to, leaving aside other affairs. The surah honors the Prophet's mission to the unlettered and criticizes those entrusted with the Torah who failed to uphold it.

Surah At-Taghaabun ('Mutual Loss and Gain') is a Medinan surah of 18 verses. It takes its name from verse 9's reference to the Day of Judgment, when people will be divided into winners and losers. The surah affirms Allah's power to create and to bring the dead back to life for judgment, and urges believers to spend in Allah's cause without being discouraged by concerns for spouses and children.

intro_en: Surah At-Talaaq ('Divorce') is a Medinan surah of 12 verses. It lays out the manner of divorce and the accommodation of divorced women and their young children, with every direction followed by the injunction to remain mindful of Allah.

intro_en: Surah At-Tahrim ('The Prohibition') is a Medinan surah of 12 verses. It addresses an incident within the Prophet's household, in which the Prophet made an oath to give up honey after two of his wives conspired to complain of a bad smell. The surah urges the believers to repent sincerely, protect their families, and take lessons from the examples of righteous and unrighteous women.

intro_en: Surah Al-Mulk ('The Sovereignty') is a Meccan surah of 30 verses. It stresses that Allah's infinite power is manifested through His perfect creation, contrasts the fate of those who deny the Resurrection with the reward of those in awe of their Lord, and affirms Allah's absolute authority.

intro_en: Surah Al-Qalam ('The Pen') is a Meccan surah of 52 verses. It opens with an oath by the pen, reassures the Prophet, and praises his outstanding character.

intro_en: Al-Haaqqa (The Reality) is a Meccan surah consisting of 52 verses. Its first section addresses the Hereafter and the Day of Judgment, while the second affirms that the Quran is a revelation from Allah and that Muhammad is His true Messenger.

intro_en: Al-Ma'aarij (The Ascending Stairways) is a Meccan surah consisting of 44 verses. It warns the disbelievers who mocked the news of the Resurrection, the Hereafter, Hell, and Paradise, answering their denial.
Nooh (Noah) is a Meccan surah consisting of 28 verses.
Al-Jinn (The Jinn) is a Meccan surah consisting of 28 verses.

Al-Muzzammil (The Enshrouded One) is a Meccan surah consisting of 20 verses. It commands the Prophet to rise at night in prayer, preparing himself to shoulder the heavy responsibilities of prophethood, and to bear his opponents' hostility with patience.
Al-Muddaththir (The Cloaked One) is a Meccan surah consisting of 56 verses.

Al-Qiyaama (The Resurrection) is a Meccan surah consisting of 40 verses. Devoted to the Resurrection itself, it addresses those who deny the Hereafter and answers their doubts about its inevitability.

sources.name: Ali Unal, The Quran with Annotated Interpretation (Modern English)

intro_en: Al-Mursalaat (The Emissaries) is a Meccan surah consisting of 50 verses. Its theme is to affirm the Resurrection and the Hereafter, and to warn of the consequences that ultimately follow denial or affirmation of these truths.

An-Naba (The Announcement) is a Meccan surah consisting of 40 verses. The whole surah is devoted to the news of Resurrection and the Hereafter, affirming it and warning of the consequences of acknowledging or disacknowledging it.

An-Naazi'aat (Those Who Drag Forth) is a Meccan surah consisting of 46 verses. It affirms the Resurrection and the life hereafter, warning of the consequences of belying the Messenger, illustrated by the story of Moses and Pharaoh.
